audience: Devin is for people who want desktop, CLI, and cloud agents on one plan and can live with a quota that is not a message count. The verdict says Pro is $20 a month, the quota is opaque, and Teams has an $80 minimum before you add seats. If you need the invoice to say how many tasks you bought, this is the wrong page.

It is a reasonable fit for a team that wants flex seats at $0 and is willing to pay the $80 floor. Flex seats draw from shared on-demand credits. A solo developer who only needs an editor should compare that $20 Pro seat with Copilot and Claude before they take the opaque quota.
features: Free is $0. Pro is $20 a month. Max is $200 a month. Teams is an $80 a month minimum plus $40 a month per full seat. Enterprise is contact sales. Docs at docs.devin.ai match these prices. That match is why the table is verified.

Desktop, CLI, and cloud agents on one plan is the pro that justifies a product this broad. Extra usage is API pricing, not a mystery credit. The included quota is the mystery. The overage unit is the clearer part, and we still do not have a per-call rate to print.

SWE-2 is free in Devin Desktop and the CLI through 16 October 2026. That is a dated promotion in the pricing note, not a permanent free agent. After that date, assume it is gone unless the docs still say it.
limitations: Included quota is not a published message count. Pro at $20 can be a bargain or a short month, and the page does not give you the number that decides which. The verdict calls that out on purpose.

Teams costs $80 even with no full seats. Full seats are $40 on top. Flex seats are $0 and still draw from the shared credits, so free seats are not free work. Do not add a headcount and forget the minimum.
The rating is Depends. Depends means the $20 Pro price is real and the amount of work inside it is not published. Max at $200 does not fix the opacity. It raises the stake.
